messages.text: The final own-tree focused run passed all 12 selected tests, including the mixed complete/incomplete-scope subtraction case. Formatting and whitespace checks are also clean. I’m submitting clippy through `cargo-slot` now; then I’ll merge the current master ref and repeat the lane checks against the merged tree.

Clippy has acquired a slot and is checking the touched crates. The plan still contains obsolete “buildq-wait” wording from the retired queue, so I’ll correct its validation record after the current-tree checks and update it again after the merge gate.

The focused tests and formatting checks are green. Clippy has progressed through the core, Python, analysis, and RQL crates; parallel lane builds are slowing completion, but the slot is running and I’m waiting for its result before touching source or merging.

The own-tree gate is green, and `master` is merged as requested. Git reported four content conflicts in the Python epoch, structural fact registry/index, and Python structural adapter; I’m reconciling both lanes’ additive facts and epoch salts now, then I’ll rerun the checks on the combined tree.

I resolved the four conflicts by preserving both Python lanes’ structural kinds and adding both fact changes to the cache-version contract (`STRUCTURAL_FACTS_VERSION=31`, index representation `7`, and both Python epoch salts). The merge commit is `d61ac697b0`; post-merge tests are running, with clippy queued.

The post-merge nextest build is recompiling the adapter and analysis crates because master changed their inputs; clippy is waiting for a slot. There are no post-merge test or lint failures so far. I also confirmed the merge retained both the parameter/binding/export work and master’s Python comparison/comment/syntax-error facts.

The combined-tree checks are still in the compile phase, rebuilding dependencies changed by master; both commands remain active and the logs show no errors. Once they finish, I’ll record the final validation in the ExecPlan and hand back the final merge SHA.

The post-merge test build has reached `brokk-bifrost-rql`; the current log still has no failure markers. The lane’s existing tests already passed before the merge, so this run is specifically validating the merged Python adapter changes and the new comparison-chain behavior.

The post-merge build is still compiling the larger analysis test binary through the slot wrapper; it has emitted no diagnostics or failures. Clippy is queued behind other lanes. I’m keeping the commands alive rather than interrupting the validation run.

Post-merge nextest passed all 14 selected tests, including both Python comparison tests from master and all binding/export regressions. Clippy has now acquired a slot and is checking the merged crates.
Clippy is checking the merged analysis crate now, with no warnings or errors reported so far. The shared-version bumps and the merged Python adapter were included in the post-merge test pass.

Post-merge clippy passed on the touched crates with `-D warnings`. The merged focused suite is 14/14 green; I’m saving the final format/whitespace evidence and updating the ExecPlan with the completed merge gate before handback.

While I was finishing validation, the shared `master` ref advanced from `570bc5693c` to `1f73a8ed44`. I’m checking and merging that newer tip too, as required by the lane procedure; this means I’ll rerun the focused tests and clippy on the new combined tree.

The newer `master` tip (`1f73a8ed44`) merged cleanly and brings in py05’s import-site relations. I’ll include py05’s import-site behavior and query-schema tests in the final focused run alongside the lane and Python-comparison tests.

The latest merge triggered one formatting finding in py05’s test module declaration order; I applied rustfmt to that file. The expanded 17-test run is queued through `cargo-slot` and will cover py02 relations plus py05 imports.

The `cargo-slot` request is waiting for the shared build slots; it has not started cargo yet. The worktree is otherwise clean apart from the one rustfmt fix, and the latest `master` tip remains an ancestor of the merged lane tree.
I committed the one-line rustfmt correction (`9c3d374ff8`) before the latest test run began. The slot request remains queued; no source or test failures have appeared.
The latest combined run acquired a slot and is compiling the analysis test binary; the queue delay was about four minutes. It is now progressing, with no diagnostics so far.

The latest run has compiled the analysis and flow crates and is actively compiling RQL tests. The Python import-site tests are in the same selection, so this validates py05’s consumer alongside the export facts.

The latest combined run passed all 17 tests, including the py05 import-site query and both master comparison tests. I’m running clippy on that tree now, then I’ll make the final format check and verify whether master advanced again.
The final workspace format check passed after the py05 module-order fix. The latest 17-test run is green; clippy is queued while the other two build slots remain occupied.
No clippy output yet; the `cargo-slot` wrapper is still waiting rather than running cargo. The final test and format evidence are saved, and I’m keeping the clippy request pending until a slot opens.
The final clippy request is queued behind three other lanes: a long Rust matrix run, py04 clippy, and py03 tests. I’m leaving their jobs alone and keeping py02 clippy queued until a slot opens.

The final 17-test run is green, and the formatting correction is committed. Clippy remains the only pending gate; the earlier transient test failures are understood and fixed, with the final passing tests covering those cases.

The latest clippy finally acquired a slot after roughly 12 minutes and is checking the analysis crate. The 17-test and final format gates remain green; I’ll finish clippy before reporting the final SHA.
Clippy has moved through analysis and is now checking flow and RQL. No warnings or errors have appeared; I’m waiting for its completion result.

All final gates are green on the current master ancestry: 17/17 focused nextest tests, clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace format check, and whitespace check. `master` is still at `1f73a8ed44`; I’m recording that final gate in the ExecPlan and then handing back the final SHA.

Understood. I’ll merge the new master tip and reconcile the shared version constants to the next values if our facts and py03’s facts both change those caches. Then I’ll rerun the 17 focused tests and clippy before handback.

I’ll merge the new master tip, reconcile structural-fact and index versions with py03’s additions, then rerun the focused tests and clippy through `cargo-slot`. I’ll also refresh the ExecPlan and handback evidence with the final combined-tree commit.

The merge has three expected overlaps: both lanes advanced the structural-facts and index versions, and py02/py03 each extended Python’s supported structural kinds. I’m preserving all merged capabilities and advancing the shared versions to 32/8 for the parameter facts added by py02.

The merge is conflict-free now, and formatting plus whitespace checks are clean. The structural versions are 32/8, with py02’s `Parameter` support and py03’s regex kinds retained together. I’m starting the 17 focused tests on this combined tree now.

The slot is running the focused suite on the merged tree; it has compiled the shared analysis and Python crates and has not reported a failure. I’m waiting for nextest to finish before launching clippy.

Nextest is still compiling the analysis crate and remains inside the build slot; there is no test failure output yet. I’ll keep the build sequential as required by the lane procedure, then run clippy with the same slot wrapper.
The remaining rebuild includes `brokk-bifrost-flow`, a broad dependency of the analysis tests. The slot is active, so I’m letting that compile complete rather than starting overlapping Cargo work.

The analysis build has advanced to `brokk-bifrost-rql`. The earlier quiet period was compilation time; there are no reported failures. Once these focused tests pass, I’ll run clippy and refresh the handback record.
All 17 focused tests passed on the merged tree (`17 passed, 6378 skipped`). I’m now running clippy with warnings denied across the touched core, Python, analysis, and RQL crates.

Clippy has started checking the touched crates and their dependency graph; it has reported no warnings or errors so far. The test build is already warm, so this should finish faster than the first compile.
Clippy remains active on the analysis crate, with no diagnostics emitted. I’m letting the validation finish before recording and committing the final merged state.

The 17 focused tests and warnings-as-errors clippy both pass on the merged tree. I’m updating the py02 ExecPlan and evidence report to record the new master tip and 32/8 versions, then I’ll commit the merge resolution and hand back the final SHA.

The merge is committed as `43759c3c16`; it has `485c59db21` as its second parent. I’m checking that the worktree is clean and master has not moved, then I’ll submit the handback with the final SHA, validation evidence, and fixed test-iteration failures.
Handed back commit `43759c3c162605ce07fc19aeb7fc819ce0c42efc`, merged with master `485c59db21`. The 17 focused tests, clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed.

I’ll continue in the py02 worktree: first merge the specified master tip and review the newly landed local-flow/assignment facts, then build the remaining policy fixtures and undefined-placeholder rule on those query relations. I’ll keep undefined cases typed-incomplete where class-template, cross-module global, or monkey-patched-builtin facts are unavailable, run the focused tests and clippy via `cargo-slot`, and land a new handback commit.

The specified master tip fast-forwarded cleanly to `c646450b87`; the worktree had no uncommitted changes. The campaign records confirm four fixtures exist but still use deliberately weak probes. I’m tracing the new initialization/CFG APIs and the policy-test harness now so the undefined-placeholder query uses existing evidence and the shadow/global fixtures assert only supported cases.

The merged `c646450b87` tree is the starting point. I’m checking the current APIs and lane validation rules, then I’ll add the CFG-backed placeholder rule and strengthen the global/shadow policy fixtures before running the focused gate through `cargo-slot`.

The flow API already has the exact three-way proof we need: initialized on all modeled paths, possibly uninitialized, or open. I’m grounding the new rule in exact identifier/read-event identity and lexical binding scope, so unsupported module/class/builtin cases remain incomplete instead of being treated as findings.

I’ve confirmed the policy layer can retain exact occurrence anchors while filtering on lexical rows: directive rows expose their source name and enclosing symbol, and binding rows carry module-scope identity. I’m updating those four campaign policies to use the new relations, then wiring the placeholder query to exact binding/read joins and the per-read CFG initialization proof.

The core relation and policy selectors are now in place. The new operator accepts exact value-reference rows, resolves their lexical binding, and only emits a finding when its source identity matches one CFG read and that read is proven possibly uninitialized. Module/class/global/builtin and unresolved cases produce incomplete diagnostics. I’m formatting the combined tree now, then I’ll let the focused tests expose any API or query-shape mismatches.

I’m continuing from the focused policy run already waiting for a cargo slot. Once it completes, I’ll fix any lane-owned failures, run the required public-query coverage and clippy, then commit and hand the receipt to the parent.
The slot is compiling the analysis crate now; no test output or failure has appeared yet. I’m letting that build finish and will keep the validation within cargo-slot.

The build is compiling the full root test target and language crates, with no diagnostics so far. This is the first compile in the lane’s current target state; I’m waiting for it to finish before selecting the follow-up checks.

The first compiler error is a single wrong module path for the occurrence row type; the actual row lives under `occurrence_rows`. Cargo is still draining its parallel compile jobs, so I’ll apply that mechanical fix as soon as this run exits, then retry the focused gate.

The first attempt finished with that type-path compile error; I fixed the path. The retry is waiting because all four machine-wide cargo slots are occupied by other lane/CI builds. While it waits, I’m checking the new public RQL step’s registry coverage and reviewing the pending diff.

The retry has the slot and has progressed past the RQL compile unit into the root dependency build. I also added the new operation to the Python tutorial coverage assertion, so the required public-step gate will verify it is exercised in the tutorial.

The test run compiled and reached all three focused tests, but each test was blocked at policy parsing rather than feature behavior. Balance checks isolated one missing outer `)` in the redundant-global, unused-global, and undefined-placeholder policy fixtures; the local-shadow-global fixture is balanced. I’m correcting those fixture delimiters before rerunning.
The rerun has acquired a slot after about three minutes waiting and is recompiling the root crate because the policy fixture text is compile-time included. Formatting and whitespace checks pass.

The failing completeness diagnostics expose a Python scope-model bug: `block` rows are being treated as lexical scopes, so an assignment inside an `if` is invisible after the block, contrary to Python function-local semantics. I’m correcting the Python adapter’s scope formation (retaining function/class/comprehension scopes) and adding a regression check; the uninitialized rule can then join its binder and CFG read without guessing.

The Python-feature build is progressing through `brokk-bifrost-analysis`, flow, and RQL. The block-scope correction now maps assignments and imports to the containing Python function scope, while comprehension scopes remain unchanged.

Compilation is still active with no diagnostics. This gate includes both the analysis crate’s Python-scope regression and the three policy cases, under the Python feature needed by the policy harness.

The analysis compile that looked idle is actively using about one core; the `mbx-rustc` process is reading the compiler’s pipe while rustc builds `brokk-bifrost-analysis`. It is not blocked in slot admission, so I’m letting it complete.

`brokk-bifrost-analysis` is still compiling and has accumulated over six minutes of rustc CPU time, with no error output. This is the expensive first build for the Python-feature test target; I’m leaving it running rather than interrupting it.
The analysis compiler has about 7½ minutes of CPU time and 7.4 GB RSS; the container is below its 68 GB limit, and rustc is still running. No test result is available yet.

The event dump showed why exact byte equality missed valid reads: the CFG lowers a condition’s read to the containing `if` span. I’ve tightened the join to accept a containing event site only when its flow subject maps to the exact lexical binder and it belongs to the same procedure/file; duplicate candidates remain typed-incomplete. For the module-global policy, the query now filters directive scopes and projects to the containing file, since policy evidence does not accept lexical-scope rows directly.

I’ll continue from the latest policy and binding-use edits, verify the lane instructions and current tree, then run the focused suite and clippy through `cargo-slot`. After that I’ll merge any newer master changes, commit this lane’s files, and hand back the report.

The latest tree is exactly at master `c646450b87`; no additional merge is needed yet. Formatting and whitespace checks are clean. The focused policy run is still waiting or compiling through `cargo-slot`, so I’m letting that owned command finish before starting any other Cargo work.
